segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Nineteen. In any triangle, the greater angle is subtended by the greater side. Given triangle A B C with angle A B C greater than angle B C A, we prove that side A C is greater than side A B.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Nineteen. In any triangle, the greater angle is subtended by the greater side. Given triangle A B C with angle A B C greater than angle B C A, we prove that side A C is greater than side A B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Suppose side A C is not greater than side A B. Then A C is either equal to A B or less than A B.

subsegments.text: Suppose side A C is not greater than side A B. Then A C is either equal to A B or less than A B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Side A C cannot equal A B, for then base angle A B C would equal angle A C B, contradicting our hypothesis. Nor can side A C be less than A B, for then angle A B C would be less than angle A C B, since the greater side subtends the greater angle. Since side A C is neither equal to nor less than A B, side A C is greater than side A B, as was required to prove.
